speaker: Ange Postecoglou
quote_text:
How do you assess the performance? Yeah, tough  game. Always is when you come here, obviously.  
It was tight, we had to fight hard to stay in  it, which I think we did fairly well. Obviously,  
Vic's pulled off a big save and we had to defend  pretty strongly at times. Always a threat going  
the other way, maybe a little bit, should  have been a little bit more clinical in that  
front third, but I thought we were in the game  and then we just conceded a really poor goal,  
which we've been doing too often. It's costing  us and that's really disappointing. But I thought  
our response from that was really good, positive.  You know, we obviously, you know, we did equalise  
and then obviously that got ruled out and then we  had a couple of big chances towards the end. So,  
yeah, really disappointed to not get something  out of the game. I'm just going to ask you  
about a specific incident where the fans seem to  taunt you when you made a substitution, then when  
Pape Sarr scored it looks like he's scored the  goal, then it looked like you sort of cupped you  
ears towards the fans as if to say what's happened  just now they've just scored. Now it's ruled out,  
can you just help talk us through your  thinking? Geez mate, it's incredible how  
things get interpreted. We just scored, I just  wanted to hear them cheer because I mean we've  
been through a tough time and I thought it was a  cracking goal and I just, I was I wanted them to  
get really excited because I felt at that point we  could potentially go on and win the game. I just  
felt momentum was on our way. It doesn't bother  me that it's not the first time they've booed  
my substitutions or my decisions. That's fine,  they're allowed to do that, but we just scored a  
goal, we just scored equalised. I was just hoping  that we could get some excitement. People want to  
read into that, that somehow I'm trying to make a  point about something. I said, I felt, you know,  
we've been through a tough time, but I just felt  there was a bit of a momentum shift there and if  
I can get really behind the lads, I thought we  had the momentum to finish on top of them. You  
don't feel that? is in danger of alienating the  fans, putting them on the powerful. Oh, look,  
John, you know what? I am at such a disconnect  with the world these days that who knows, mate,  
maybe you're right. I don't know, but that's not  what my intention was. Did you think it was a  
foul? But see, that's the problem. Whether I think  it's a foul or not, what does it matter? What  
matters is VAR was called in for clear and obvious  errors, right? I've said this a few times already.  
We all sat on our couches last night and watched  an incident where I reckon if I did a poll in this  
room, I said, after the first replay, what did you  think? How long did it take tonight? Six minutes  
for a clear and obvious error. Like, whether it's  a foul, who cares if it's a foul or not? There's  
so many incidents that are very similar out there.  Now they say, oh, well, this becomes a goal,  
but what does it matter? What's the point of  having a referee then? Like, clear and obvious  
to me is you go to the screen, you say, oh my God,  I've missed that. Let's go. Standing around for,  
I mean, if, but that's, but we're all, not  me, because I'm very vocal about it, everyone  
accepts it. That's where, that's, it's going to  be refereed by AI pretty soon. I say we might as  
well dispense of the players at some point, some  kind of come up with a genius way of just having  
a game of football with no participants, because  referees aren't refereeing. Like I said, to me,  
if anyone believes that when VAR was brought in,  that we would be sitting around for six minutes,  
with a microscope. It's irrelevant whether it's  a foul or not. It's totally irrelevant. And  
they're going to say, well, we came to the right  decision. But that's irrelevant because there's  
so many other decisions out there that are always  lying ball that will do that for everyone. Now,  
Jarred Gillett was on VAR tonight. Maybe if Jarred  Gillett was on VAR last night, there would have  
been a different outcome. Because again, it comes  down, I guess, to everyone's interpretation. But  
I don't like it, mate. I never liked it. I don't  see how it's benefiting our game. I don't think  
anyone would have complained tonight if we just  went with referees' decisions. You get some good,  
you get some bad, you get on with it, but the game  finishes in 93, 94 minutes. The game flows instead  
of us sitting around and doing what I don't know.  But like I said, I think that's one bit that won't  
get misinterpreted by me. I'm pretty consistent  on my stance on it. And the fans didn't know,  
but they did see some of them saying, you  don't know what you're doing, and it's quite  
clear. That's the first time I've heard them sing  without you. Did that hurt? Again, Matt, like I,  
I don't know, it's just doesn't, it doesn't  affect me if that's what the fans feel, and  
if they feel that I'm not doing a good job, then  they've got every right to express that they play,  
they're hard and they follow the club, they're  the ones that will be here long after I'm gone,  
so it doesn't, it doesn't, it doesn't affect me.  What I kind of try and focus on is the things I  
can control. I can't control fans, I can't control  many things, but I can control our football and  
the way we play and the way we conduct ourselves  and that's what I concentrate on. Thank you.
title: Ange Postecoglou post-match press conference | Chelsea 1-0 Tottenham Hotspur
